natsUserConfig.namePlaceholder: Enter the name of your NATS User
natsUserConfig.nameHint: Friendly label for this credential. Often one NATS user per app or service.
natsUserConfig.signingGroupHint: Signing group that issues the user JWT. Scoped groups can inherit default publish/subscribe limits.
natsUserConfig.tagsHint: Optional labels for filtering and ops (e.g. team or env). Not used for auth by themselves.
natsUserConfig.permissionsLead: Add or remove permissions for this NATS entity
natsUserConfig.publishHint: Subjects this user may publish to. Empty allow = unrestricted publish unless deny rules apply. Prefer least privilege.
natsUserConfig.subscribeHint: Subjects this user may subscribe to. Empty allow = unrestricted subscribe unless deny rules apply.
natsUserConfig.unrestrictedPublish: This user has unrestricted access to publish
natsUserConfig.unrestrictedSubscribe: This user has unrestricted access to subscribe
natsUserConfig.limitsLead: Configure the limits for your NATS Resource
natsUserConfig.maxSubsHint: Cap concurrent subscriptions per connection. Leave unlimited unless you need to protect the server.
natsUserConfig.maxPayloadHint: Largest message this user may publish. Match your largest expected payload; leave unlimited for general clients.
natsUserConfig.jwtLifetimeHint: How long the minted JWT stays valid. Shorter lifetimes reduce leak risk; longer ones need fewer remints.
natsUserConfig.maxDataHint: Total bytes this user may have in flight / pending. Leave unlimited unless enforcing quotas.
natsUserConfig.advancedLead: Bearer auth, connection types, source CIDRs, time windows, and response permissions
natsUserConfig.bearerTokenHint: Skip nonce signing (token-only auth). Prefer off for interactive clients; on only for constrained environments that require it.
natsUserConfig.proxyRequiredHint: Require connections through an authorized proxy. Use when clients must not connect directly to NATS.
natsUserConfig.connectionTypesHint: Restrict client protocols (STANDARD, WEBSOCKET, MQTT, etc.). Empty = all types allowed.
natsUserConfig.srcCidrsHint: Only allow connections from these networks. Use for private VPC or office ranges.
natsUserConfig.timeRestrictionsHint: Limit when this user may connect. Set an IANA timezone plus start/end times (HH:MM:SS).
natsUserConfig.responsePermsHint: Allow temporary replies to inbox subjects after a valid subscribe. Cap max replies and TTL for request/reply clients.

jetstream.title: JetStream
jetstream.subtitle: Manage Streams, Mirrors, KV Buckets and Object Stores for this account
jetstream.lifecycleHint: After create, you can edit or delete streams, mirrors, KV buckets, and object stores — open the resource for Edit config, or use Delete on the list or detail page. Consumers are edited or deleted from the consumer detail page.
jetstream.empty: No streams found. Click Create Stream to create one.

kvConfig.basicInfoLead: Configure the basic properties of your KV Bucket.
kvConfig.nameHint: Unique bucket name in this account. Cannot be renamed after create.
kvConfig.descriptionPlaceholder: A short description of the KV Bucket
kvConfig.replicasHint: Odd count for HA. Use 1 for single-node; 3 for production clusters.
kvConfig.storageHint: File persists to disk; Memory is faster but lost on restart. Prefer File for durable data.
kvConfig.storeSettingsLead: Properties settings for a KV bucket
kvConfig.historyHint: Revisions kept per key (1–64). Use >1 when you need watchers or rollback.
kvConfig.ttlHint: Expire keys after this duration (e.g. 1h, 7d). Leave off to keep values forever.
kvConfig.maxValueSizeHint: Reject puts larger than this. Match your largest expected value.
kvConfig.maxBytesHint: Cap total bucket size. Pair with TTL or deletes so the store cannot fill forever.
kvConfig.placementLead: Configure where your KV Bucket is stored.
kvConfig.clusterHint: Pin the bucket to a named JetStream cluster. Leave off for default placement.
kvConfig.tagsHint: Server placement tags (e.g. ssd, geo). Servers must advertise matching tags.
kvConfig.advancedLead: Compression, delete markers, republish, mirror/sources, and metadata.
kvConfig.compressionHint: S2-compress the backing stream (nats-server 2.10+). Saves disk at some CPU cost.
kvConfig.limitMarkerTTLHint: How long delete/TTL markers are kept. Needed for per-key TTL watchers (min ~1s).
kvConfig.republishHint: Also publish each put to another subject. Handy for side processing or fan-out.
kvConfig.mirrorHint: Mirror another KV/stream into this bucket. Usually set at create time.
kvConfig.sourcesHint: Aggregate keys from other streams/buckets (optional filter subject).
kvConfig.metadataHint: Arbitrary key/value labels for operators or tooling.

objectConfig.basicInfoLead: Configure the basic properties of your Object Bucket.
objectConfig.nameHint: Unique bucket name in this account. Cannot be renamed after create.
objectConfig.descriptionPlaceholder: A short description of the Object Bucket
objectConfig.replicasHint: Odd count for HA. Use 1 for single-node; 3 for production clusters.
objectConfig.storageHint: File persists to disk; Memory is faster but lost on restart. Prefer File for durable objects.
objectConfig.storeSettingsLead: Retention and size limits for objects in this bucket.
objectConfig.maxAgeHint: Expire objects after this duration (e.g. 1h, 7d). Leave off to keep objects forever.
objectConfig.maxBytesHint: Cap total bucket size. Pair with Max age or deletes so the store cannot fill forever.
objectConfig.placementLead: Configure where your Object Bucket is stored.
objectConfig.clusterHint: Pin the bucket to a named JetStream cluster. Leave off for default placement.
objectConfig.tagsHint: Server placement tags (e.g. ssd, geo). Servers must advertise matching tags.
objectConfig.advancedLead: Compression and metadata for the backing Object Store stream.
objectConfig.compressionHint: S2-compress the backing stream (nats-server 2.10+). Saves disk at some CPU cost.
objectConfig.metadataHint: Arbitrary key/value labels for operators or tooling.

streamConfig.basicInfoLead: Configure the basic properties of your Stream.
streamConfig.nameHint: Unique stream name in this account. Cannot be renamed after create.
streamConfig.descriptionPlaceholder: A short description of the Stream
streamConfig.descriptionHint: Optional human-readable note for operators. Not used by JetStream runtime.
streamConfig.replicasHint: Odd count for HA. Use 1 for single-node; 3 for production clusters.
streamConfig.storageHint: File persists to disk; Memory is faster but lost on restart. Prefer File for durable data.
streamConfig.compressionHint: S2 compresses stored messages to save disk. Use None for lowest CPU or already-compressed payloads.
streamConfig.mirrorSourceLead: Choose the stream this mirror copies from, and optional start/filter options.
streamConfig.mirrorSourceNameHint: Name of the origin stream to mirror. Required; subjects are not used on mirrors.
streamConfig.mirrorFilterHint: Optional subject filter so only matching messages are mirrored.
streamConfig.mirrorStartSeqHint: Begin mirroring from this sequence on the source. Leave off to start from the beginning.
streamConfig.mirrorStartTimeHint: Begin mirroring from this RFC3339 timestamp on the source.
streamConfig.mirrorExternalHint: API and deliver prefixes for mirroring a stream from another account or leaf node.
streamConfig.subjectsLead: Configure the subjects that this stream will persist messages for. Wildcards are permitted.
streamConfig.subjectsHint: Subjects (and wildcards) this stream captures. Prefer narrow patterns over > unless you intend a catch-all.
streamConfig.noSubjects: No subjects have been set for this stream
streamConfig.retentionLead: Policies around retention and discarding of messages in this stream.
streamConfig.policyHint: Limits = delete by age/size; Interest = drop when no consumers; WorkQueue = each message consumed once.
streamConfig.discardPolicyHint: Old = drop oldest when full; New = reject new publishes when full. Prefer Old for continuous ingestion.
streamConfig.allowRollupsHint: Permit rollup headers to replace subject history. Enable for KV-like latest-value patterns.
streamConfig.allowDeletionHint: Allow API deletion of individual messages. Disable for append-only / audit streams.
streamConfig.allowPurgingHint: Allow purge of subjects or the whole stream. Keep on for ops; off for immutable ledgers.
streamConfig.discardNewPerSubjectHint: With discard=new, apply the limit per subject instead of stream-wide. Use with max msgs per subject.
streamConfig.limitsLead: Configure limits for consumers, streams, messages and subjects.
streamConfig.maxAgeHint: Drop messages older than this (e.g. 1h, 7d). Primary retention knob for time-based cleanup.
streamConfig.maxBytesHint: Cap total stored bytes. Pair with discard policy when the stream can fill.
streamConfig.maxConsumersHint: Cap how many consumers can attach. Leave unlimited unless enforcing tenancy.
streamConfig.maxMsgSizeHint: Reject publishes larger than this. Match your largest payload; default server limits apply if off.
streamConfig.maxMsgsHint: Cap total messages in the stream. Useful with workqueues or bounded buffers.
streamConfig.maxMsgsPerSubjectHint: Keep at most N messages per subject. Use for last-N or sensor-style subjects.
streamConfig.placementLead: Configure where your Stream is stored.
streamConfig.clusterHint: Pin the stream to a named JetStream cluster. Leave off for default placement.
streamConfig.tagsHint: Server placement tags (e.g. ssd, geo). Servers must advertise matching tags.
streamConfig.advancedLead: Compression, duplicates, sources, transforms, and other JetStream options.
streamConfig.duplicatesHint: Deduplicate publishes with the same Nats-Msg-Id within this window (e.g. 2m). Default ~2m is typical.
streamConfig.allowDirectHint: Allow direct get-by-sequence/subject without a consumer. Useful for KV-style and admin reads.
streamConfig.mirrorDirectHint: Allow direct gets against mirror sources. Enable when clients read through a mirror.
streamConfig.allowMsgTTLHint: Honor per-message TTL headers. Use when publishers set expiry on individual messages.
streamConfig.noAckHint: Treat publishes as fire-and-forget (no pub ack). Rare; prefer off for reliable ingestion.
streamConfig.sealedWarning: Sealing is irreversible — the stream cannot be unsealed later.
streamConfig.sealedHint: Freeze the stream against further changes. Only for end-of-life archival.
streamConfig.firstSeqHint: Start numbering at this sequence (advanced migration). Leave off for normal streams.
streamConfig.markerTTLHint: How long subject-delete markers are retained. Relevant with interest retention and delete markers.
streamConfig.subjectTransformHint: Rewrite stored subject using source/dest patterns. Use to normalize or namespace subjects on ingest.
streamConfig.republishHint: Also publish a copy to another subject on ingest. Handy for fan-out or side processing.
streamConfig.headersOnlyHint: Republish headers without the payload. Use for lightweight notifications.
streamConfig.consumerLimitsHint: Default caps applied to new consumers on this stream.
streamConfig.inactiveThresholdHint: Delete idle consumers after this duration (e.g. 1m). Helps clean abandoned consumers.
streamConfig.maxAckPendingHint: Max unacked messages per consumer. Lower values reduce memory; raise for high throughput.
streamConfig.sourcesLead: Source messages from other streams (optional filter subject).
streamConfig.sourcesHint: Aggregate from other streams into this one. Optional filter narrows which subjects are copied.
streamConfig.metadataHint: Arbitrary key/value labels for operators or tooling. Not enforced by JetStream.

liveStream.title: Live: {{name}}
liveStream.clientHint: Live is a console viewer only (ephemeral push over WebSocket). App clients should bind a durable pull consumer on the stream, then subscribe with filter subjects — not this Live session.

consumer.clientRecommend: For NATS clients: create a durable pull consumer (leave Deliver subject empty), set Filter subjects to the stream subjects you need, then pull/consume from your app. Use push only when you need a deliver subject or a deliver group for shared workers. Consumers can be edited or deleted from the consumer detail page.

consumerConfig.recommendBody: Prefer a durable pull consumer: leave Deliver subject empty, set Filter subjects to match the stream (e.g. orders.> ), then in your client bind that durable and pull or consume. Use push only when you need server delivery to a subject, or a deliver group for load-balanced workers. Do not use the console Live tab as an application subscription.
consumerConfig.recommendBodyStream: Durable pull `{{durable}}`{{filters}}. Deliver policy all (switch to new for live-only traffic), ack {{ack}}. Leave Deliver subject empty. Apply fills this form — then save and bind the durable from your NATS client.
consumerConfig.basicInfoLead: Name and storage options for this consumer.
consumerConfig.durableNameHint: Stable name your NATS client binds to (pull/push). Cannot be renamed after create.
consumerConfig.descriptionPlaceholder: A short description of the consumer
consumerConfig.replicasHint: Override consumer replica count. Leave inherit for stream default.
consumerConfig.memoryStorageHint: Keep consumer state in memory instead of file storage.
consumerConfig.deliveryLead: Where delivery starts and which subjects are consumed.
consumerConfig.deliverPolicyHint: all/last/new from stream start; by_start_* for a cursor; last_per_subject for latest per subject.
consumerConfig.ackPolicyHint: explicit = ack each message; all = ack cumulative; none = no acks.
consumerConfig.replayPolicyHint: instant replays as fast as possible; original preserves original timing.
consumerConfig.filterSubjectsHint: Subjects (and wildcards) this consumer reads from the stream. Match what your client should receive.
consumerConfig.ackRedeliveryLead: How long to wait for acks and how retries behave.
consumerConfig.ackWaitHint: Time before an unacked message is redelivered (e.g. 30s).
consumerConfig.maxDeliverHint: Max delivery attempts including the first. Use with backoff for poison messages.
consumerConfig.backoffHint: Redelivery delays after each failed attempt (e.g. 1s, 5s, 30s).
consumerConfig.maxAckPendingHint: Max in-flight unacked messages for this consumer.
consumerConfig.pullLead: Recommended for most app clients. Tune pull request limits here (ignored when a deliver subject is set).
consumerConfig.maxWaitingHint: Max outstanding pull requests waiting for messages.
consumerConfig.maxRequestBatchHint: Cap batch size on pull requests.
consumerConfig.maxRequestExpiresHint: Max expiry a pull request may request.
consumerConfig.maxRequestMaxBytesHint: Cap total bytes returned in a single pull response.
consumerConfig.pushLead: Use only when clients need push delivery. Leave deliver subject empty to stay on pull.
consumerConfig.deliverSubjectHint: Leave empty for pull (recommended). Set an inbox/deliver subject only for push consumers.
consumerConfig.deliverGroupHint: Queue group so multiple push clients share work. Ignored for pull.
consumerConfig.flowControlHint: Enable push flow control so slow consumers do not overwhelm the connection.
consumerConfig.advancedLead: Rate limiting, sampling, inactivity, and metadata.
consumerConfig.rateLimitHint: Throttle delivery in bits per second.
consumerConfig.inactiveThresholdHint: Delete the consumer after this idle duration (e.g. 1h).
consumerConfig.metadataHint: Arbitrary key/value labels for operators or tooling.
consumerConfig.optStartSeqRequired: Start sequence is required for by_start_sequence
consumerConfig.optStartTimeRequired: Start time is required for by_start_time
